records.reason: Hebron is a city context for Mamre, not an exact patriarchal event point.

contextNote.en: Aelia Capitolina was founded under Hadrian around AD 130. That name must not be projected onto Jerusalem during Christ’s Passion.
contextNote.fr: Aelia Capitolina est le nom de la ville refondée sous Hadrien, vers 130 apr. J.-C. Il ne convient pas pour la Jérusalem de la Passion.

records.sourceCaveat: Hadrianic refoundation chronology, not Pleiades broad name date.

records.reason: Multiple occupation periods and settlement positions; a transliteration adds no useful historical distinction here.
The existing Biblical form suffices; the source does not justify a new historically distinct public label.
Kefar Nahum and Kapharnaoum are language variants, not a demonstrated chronological change in place identity.

contextNote.en: Samaria was the capital established by Omri. Herod later rebuilt the city and called it Sebaste; that later name must not label the Israelite kingdom.
contextNote.fr: Samarie fut la capitale fondée par Omri. Hérode reconstruisit plus tard la ville et l’appela Sébaste : ce nom ne convient pas à l’époque du royaume d’Israël.

records.sourceCaveat: Samaria the city and Samaria the region are distinct; Sebaste date evidence supersedes narrow Pleiades export.

contextNote.en: Herod transformed the older Strato’s Tower into Caesarea. The Caesarea of Acts is the rebuilt Roman-period port, not the earlier settlement under its former name.
contextNote.fr: Hérode transforma l’ancienne tour de Straton en Césarée. La Césarée des Actes est le port reconstruit à l’époque romaine, non l’établissement ancien sous son premier nom.

records.sourceCaveat: Caesarea Maritima is retained as bilingual disambiguator, not a literal Gospel/Acts quotation.

contextNote.en: Ioppe is a Greek-form name for Joppa in ancient geographical records; older Near Eastern records preserve other forms. The map keeps the familiar Biblical name.
contextNote.fr: Ioppé est une forme grecque du nom de Joppé dans les sources géographiques anciennes ; des formes plus anciennes sont aussi attestées. La carte conserve le nom biblique familier.

records.sourceCaveat: Language variants are not evidence of a formal city renaming or exact event site.

contextNote.en: Ninuwā is an ancient Mesopotamian form of Nineveh’s name. It is a linguistic reference, not a precise date or archaeological location for Jonah’s account.
contextNote.fr: Ninuwā est une forme mésopotamienne ancienne du nom de Ninive. Elle indique une tradition linguistique, non une date précise ni le lieu exact du récit de Jonas.

records.sourceCaveat: Source corpus attests Ninua; Pleiades supplies different romanization Ninuwā. No assumed exact year for Jonah.

contextNote.en: Bābili is an ancient name for Babylon recorded in Mesopotamian sources. The English and French Biblical names remain the primary map labels.
contextNote.fr: Bābili est un ancien nom de Babylone attesté dans les sources mésopotamiennes. Les noms bibliques français et anglais restent ceux de la carte.

records.sourceCaveat: Linguistic evidence is not an exact dating of the events of exile.

records.reason: The established name already identifies the Acts setting; older Semitic variants are unnecessary on the map.

contextNote.en: Antioch on the Orontes was called Theoupolis only from AD 528, centuries after the Apostles. The New Testament setting retains Antioch.
contextNote.fr: Antioche sur l’Oronte reçut le nom de Théoupolis en 528, plusieurs siècles après les Apôtres. Pour le Nouveau Testament, on conserve Antioche.

records.sourceCaveat: Later sixth-century Christian name must not be projected into the apostolic narrative.

contextNote.en: The city had the Seleucid-era name Antioch on the Cydnus. Acts identifies St Paul’s birthplace as Tarsus, which remains the appropriate principal label.
contextNote.fr: La cité porta à l’époque séleucide le nom d’Antioche du Cydnus. Les Actes désignent la ville natale de saint Paul comme Tarse : ce nom reste principal.

records.sourceCaveat: Older secondary designation need not imply that a first-century speaker would use it.

records.reason: Athenae adds little beyond translated Athens, and the source coordinate is rough.
Arsinoeia belongs to other naming contexts; no proven need to replace Ephesus.

contextNote.en: The settlement was called Krenides before Philip II renamed it Philippi in 356 BC. St Paul visited a later Roman colony of the same name.
contextNote.fr: La ville s’appelait Krénidès avant que Philippe II ne la renomme Philippes en 356 av. J.-C. Saint Paul visita ensuite une colonie romaine.

records.sourceCaveat: The place of Acts was already Philippi, not Krenides; colony status is Roman-period contextual information.

contextNote.en: The Greek city was destroyed by Rome in 146 BC and refounded as a Roman colony in 44 BC. St Paul’s Corinth belongs to this later urban phase.
contextNote.fr: La cité grecque fut détruite par Rome en 146 av. J.-C., puis refondée en colonie romaine en 44 av. J.-C. La Corinthe de saint Paul appartient à cette seconde phase.

records.sourceCaveat: Roman refoundation is a settlement-history claim, not evidence of a unique event point.

records.reason: Roma adds no meaningful context to Rome; Pleiades city point is rough.
Existing Lystra name is appropriate; colonial title is not necessary for this event.
The existing translation is period-appropriate, so no extra name note is justified.

contextNote.en: Founded as Antigoneia about 310 BC, the city became Alexandria Troas after Lysimachus renamed it. Acts refers to it as Troas.
contextNote.fr: Fondée sous le nom d’Antigonéia vers 310 av. J.-C., la ville devint Alexandrie de Troade après son changement de nom par Lysimaque. Les Actes l’appellent Troade.

records.sourceCaveat: Antigoneia must not be used as first-century primary map label.

records.reason: Earlier settlement names are not appropriate as a primary Acts-era map label.
